{{Quote|The reptilian marauders work together in a powerful military fashion to bring terror to the Ewoks and cause damage out of sheer spite. How could we not like them?|Pfilbee Jhorn, about the Sanyassan castaways of Endor|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
The '''Sanyassans''' were a [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the stormy [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Sanyassa IV]], located in the [[Inner Zuma Region]]. They had [[Ape/Legends|ape]]-like faces, scaly skin, and a tall stature that averaged two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height. They engaged in [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]] from ancient [[Time/Legends|times]], becoming the scourge of the greater [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. In the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], these [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] had the reputation of being fierce fighters, armed with short tempers and even shorter levels of intelligence. They were sometimes employed as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] or [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], and at least one of them, [[Tun-Badon]], pledged allegiance to a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. 

When the [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] wrote his [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species|''Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] at the height of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], little was known about the Sanyassans, despite their occasionally fleeting presence in broader [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] affairs; In fact, so little was known of their species or their history, with few knowing of their [[Homeworld/Legends|home planet]], they were collectively referred to as "marauders”&mdash;or “Sanyassan marauders”&mdash;by most [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]].

On their homeworld, the Sanyassans had only achieved [[Technology level|feudal-level technology]] by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]; their most advanced development by that time was the implementation of a writing system. Like the rest of the Moddell [[Sector/Legends|sector]], the peoples of Sanyassa IV were excluded from galactic [[Politics/Legends|politics]] for most of their history. However, in the distant past, they had once been a more advanced civilization (prior to the [[Din supernova]] turning into a [[Din Pulsar/Legends|pulsar]], around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]). According to the neighboring [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] species, that event may have drastically altered the Sanyassans' way of life, causing their focus to shift from intellectual, societal growth to pure survival. Thus, after the cataclysm, their leaders established a complex caste system and social hierarchy, in which the “pecking-order” was determined by might.

In the first [[Standard century/Legends|century]] before the Galactic Civil War, a large group of Sanyassan criminals (known as the [[Sanyassan Marauders/Legends|Marauders]]) crash-landed in the [[Tree/Legends|forests]] of the [[Endor/Legends|moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]]. As they were unable to get off of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]], these Sanyassan Marauders established a colony in the [[Dragon's Pelt/Legends|Dragon's Pelt]] savanna, under the leadership of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Terak]]. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Sanyassans of Endor suffered a terrible [[Battle of Endor (Ewok–Sanyassan conflict)|defeat]] against the native [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], with their numbers then decreasing over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. When the New Republic was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|established]], the government [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] who were sent to the forest moon found no trace of them.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|The marauders have greasy, thick strands of hair - usually pale, sometimes dark - sprouting from the crown of their flat heads&hellip;occasionally from the skin on their faces. Heavy, protective brow ridges, thrust like hoods over glittering eyes&hellip;pug nose-holes give the marauders a skull-like appearance.|Pfilbee Jhorn|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
[[File:Anonymous_Sanyassan.png|thumb|upright|left|A male Sanyassan with brown skin]]
The Sanyassans were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], with [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] physical traits.<ref name="ISWU" /> They were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in form, with four [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], two legs and two arms. They had two-toed feet; the hand structure and appearance varied, with some individuals possessing three,<ref name="ISWU" /> four,<ref name="BFE" /> up to five<ref name="RFT">{{GamerCite|9|Race for the Tessent}}</ref> digits per hand (including an opposable thumb).<ref name="BFE" /> Members of this species had powerfully-built frames and grew to be quite tall, between 1.6 and 2.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="UAA" /> with an average of 2.0 meters.<ref name="EGAS" /> Sometimes, a congenital disorder resulted in [[nanism]], as exemplified by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Yavid]] (who stood only 1.1 meters tall).<ref name="dbYavid">{{DB|character|generalyavid|Yavid, General}}</ref> The Sanyassans had tougher hides than most humanoids, which made them more resistant to physical or energetic damage.<ref name="EndorModdell" /> Sanyassan skin was [[Leather/Legends|leathery]] and scaly; their varied [[Color/Legends|coloration]] included dull shades of gray, brown, green, and yellow.<ref name="ISWU" /> Though much rarer, some pale pink-<ref name="SWG" /> and purple-skinned individuals were known to exist.<ref name="KOR44" />

[[File:Female_Sanyassan.jpg|thumb|A female Sanyassan with a smoother, pinkish skin]]
According to [[Human/Legends|Human]] observers, the Sanyassans' [[Primate/Legends|simian]] faces were [[Bone/Legends|skull]]-like in appearance (the skin pulled tautly over the bones), with the [[Nose/Legends|nose]] being a mere pair of pug-like holes; their deep-set, forward-facing [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were crowned by jutting brow-ridges. Some members of the species exhibited cranial ridges on the parietal bones, and the males often sported tiny, spiky growths from the temples. They had high foreheads, and relatively small [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]], with very thin lips. The fearsome-looking Sanyassans had straggly [[Hair/Legends|manes]], that fell to the shoulders on some specimens.<ref name="UAA" /> Others were bald,<ref name="ISWU" /> some cut their hair short,<ref name="BFE" /> and others opted for a single bunch of hair styled into a top-knot. Occasionally, hair also grew from the skin of their faces, in the manner of a mustache or a beard,<ref name="ISWU" /> yet the Sanyassans had no eyebrows or eyelids.<ref name="SWG" /> The species usually had very Human-like [[Ear/Legends|ears]],<ref name="SWG" /> with some individuals possessing pointed ears,<ref name="EGAS" /> akin to those of the [[Sephi/Legends|Sephi]] species from [[Thustra/Legends|Thustra]].<ref name="JY">''[[Jedi: Yoda]]''</ref>

The species had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], male and female; Sexual dimorphism manifested, predominantly, in the presence of pronounced [[Breast/Legends|breasts]] in females. Sanyassan women also tended to have smoother skin and did not grow facial hair.<ref name="SWG" /> Considered [[Youngling/Legends|children]] until the age of eight (at which point they entered a brief adolescent period), Sanyassans attained “young adulthood” when they turned thirteen. At fourteen, they grew out of adolescence and lived out their adulthood for twenty-five [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. At forty, a Sanyassan was considered middle-aged, with he or she being viewed as “elderly” beyond the age of seventy.<ref name="UAA" /> Of course, super centenarians were not uncommon, and Sanyassans could maintain their warrior prowess even into their latter years; the [[Sanyassan Marauders/Legends|Sanyassan Marauders]] who shipwrecked on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] around [[96 BBY]] were still alive a [[Standard century/Legends|standard century]] later.<ref name="BFE" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Wh-what have you done with my friends the Ewoks?''"<br />"''Why, they're my special guests. In my dungeon, that is.|Cindel Towani and the Marauder King Terak|<ref name="The Ring, the Witch, and the Crystal: An Ewok Adventure">''[[The Ring, the Witch, and the Crystal: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Marauder_arm-wrestling.jpg|thumb|left|Two Sanyassans arm-wrestling together]]
At one point in their history, the Sanyassans were thought to have had an advanced society and culture, but those [[Standard day/Legends|days]] were long gone by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]<ref name="EndorModdell" />&mdash;a conflict fought between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> In its better known form, the Sanyassan society was divided into clanic structures&mdash;united groups of households tracing descent from a common ancestor.<ref name="UAA" /> The Sanyassans observed no law prohibiting them from preying upon others.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> There existed a form of [[Noble/Legends|aristocracy]], but social standing was gained by force, rather than birthright. The Sanyassan upper class consisted mainly of the strongest and tallest individuals and showed strong social prejudices against dwarfs.<ref name="dbYavid" />

Their culture was brutal, based on [[Ground warfare/Legends|warfare]] and exploitation of the weak. The species seemed unforgiving, ruthless and calculating to outsiders. In the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], these fierce brawlers were renowned for their bad tempers and low intellectual performance.<ref name="EndorModdell" /> Despite their aggressive nature, the Sanyassans were social beings and did not feel comfortable while alone. They preferred to be in large groups, as when marching out to raid. When not fighting, they enjoyed having arm-wrestling contests, playing cards with each other, feasting in banquet halls,<ref name="ISWU" /> and drinking [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]] while [[Toast (ritual)/Legends|clinking]] their cups together with loud guffaws.<ref name="BFE" />

On Endor, most Sanyassan commoners wore makeshift [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and ragged [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]], usually brown or cream in color, adorned with [[Scavenger/Legends|scavenged]] items<ref name="CSWESan">{{CSWECite|III|127|Sanyassan Marauders}}</ref> and patches of animal fur. Some higher-class individuals possessed more elegant attire, with [[Gold/Legends|golden]] plate pauldrons and forearm guards, flowing bluish-grey [[Cape/Legends|capes]], quilted vests and cloth belts. The Endorian Sanyassans typically wrapped their feet in rawhide or cloth and tied that on with laces for foot covering.<ref name="BFE" />

[[File:Technological_imbecile.png|thumb|A Sanyassan Marauder pouring water over a heated machine]]
Technologically primitive by [[Technology level|galactic standards]], Sanyassans formed a feudal-level civilization,<ref name="EndorModdell" /> with a crude hieroglyphic [[Writing/Legends|writing system]].<ref name="ISWU" /> They never developed the secrets of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel for themselves, but stole it from others.<ref name="UAA" /> They had a rather rudimentary grasp on technology, which caused more harm than good when they tried to use it.<ref name="ISWU" /> For instance, one of the Sanyassan Marauder [[King/Legends|King]] [[Terak]]'s [[Unidentified Sanyassan goon|goons]] once poured [[Water/Legends|water]] over an electrical device, which caused the machine to burst into sparks.<ref name="BFE" /> As the Sanyassans never achieved space travel themselves, they relied on poor instinctive [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] skills when piloting stolen [[Starship/Legends|ships]]. While they managed to keep their [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] functioning, many were battered and rusted. However, the Sanyassans were proficient in [[Sword/Legends|sword]]-fighting and [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]].<ref name="ISWU" /> Despite their poor intelligence, most Sanyassans could speak a broken form of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], in addition to their native [[Sanyassan (language)|Sanyassan]].<ref name="EndorModdell" /> Sanyassan names were typically one word, with examples including Dranjat, Jorak, Krenna, Kresho, Luryk, Maygo, S'Zingo, Terakaya, Urkreg, Vortek, and Zaykul.<ref name="UAA" /> Other known names included Bar'injar,<ref name="KOR44" /> Indar, Macchbraus,<ref name="SWG" /> and Yavid.<ref name="dbYavid" />

Sanyassans displayed a grim and sadistic sense of humor. King Terak once referred with irony to his Ewok [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] as his "friends" and "most honored guests," to which his henchmen all laughed in unison. Members of the species fed off suffering and misery, to the point of falling off their chair, laughing, when they witnessed other people's pain.<ref name="BFE" />

==History==
{{Quote|The long-lived marauders originated off-planet and crashed nearly a century ago on the Forest Moon.|Pfilbee Jhorn|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
[[File:Sanyassa_and_surroundings.png|thumb|left|Sanyassa and surrounding [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] in the Inner Zuma]]
The Sanyassans evolved on the world of [[Sanyassa IV]], a temperate [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]],<ref name="EndorModdell" /> one of the three [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] that made up the [[Inner Zuma Region]] of the [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Like the rest of the worlds in the sector, Sanyassa IV was ignored by the wider [[galactic community]] for most of its history, as it was considered a part of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] until the last centuries of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> Millennia before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the original Sanyassans were a much more advanced society than their descendants. Through time, the Sanyassan culture devolved into a might-makes-right kleptocracy.<ref name="EndorModdell" /> According to the [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]], a peaceful species from the nearby world [[Maya Kovel/Legends|Maya Kovel]], that devolution may have been the consequence of the [[Din supernova]] that led to the creation of a [[Din Pulsar/Legends|pulsar]] around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> a cataclysm from which the Sanyassans never fully recovered.<ref name="EndorModdell" />

For most of their recorded history, the brutal Sanyassans were renowned in their native sector as raiders and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]].<ref name="EndorModdell" /> In the first century before [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY's]] [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], one such band of Sanyassan criminals known as the [[Sanyassan Marauders/Legends|Marauders]] crashed on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]]. As their ship was damaged beyond repair, the Marauders settled on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="ISWU" /> The name "Marauders" was later used as a generic name to describe the entire species, even amongst [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]].<ref name="EGAS" />

==Sanyassans in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Because their true name is unknown, this species is referred to in scientific circles simply as Marauders.|Mammon Hoole|<ref name="EGAS" />}}
[[File:Sanyassan_marauder_concept_art.png|upright|thumb|A Sanyassan thug]]
In the fourth millennium before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], a male Sanyassan known as [[Bar'injar]] joined [[the Crucible]], a [[Slavery/Legends|slave-trading]] organization<ref name="KOR44" /> founded many years before by [[Ieldis]]&mdash;a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Old Empire]].<ref name="KE">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref> During the later stages of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], an ancient [[Credit chip/Legends|credit chip]] coming from the treasure hoards of a long-departed [[Unidentified Sanyassan warlord|Sanyassan warlord]] was found. That discovery prompted certain galactic citizens to use their [[Slicer/Legends|slicing]] skills in hopes of tracing the chip back to the rest of the treasure.<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Slicing|Loose Change}}</ref>

However, despite their occasional presence abroad, the Sanyassans were not well known outside their native Moddell sector: millennia later, during the height of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], [[Sentientologist|Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] was still researching the species. Although his notes on Sanyassans were far from complete, Hoole felt they were worth mentioning in ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', a [[Book/Legends|guidebook]] based on his collected data. In his sketchy notes, Hoole used the nickname "Marauders" for the entire species, as he claimed their true name was unknown, even in [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] circles. Hoole also made no mention of which planet it was from which the Sanyassans hailed.<ref name="EGAS" />

Members of other species knew how to take advantage of the Sanyassans' cruel nature. The brutish humanoids were armed with the latest weapons and employed as [[Shock trooper/Legends|shock troopers]] or petty thugs.<ref name="UAA" /> During the [[Republic Dark Age]], the male Sanyassan [[Tun-Badon]] commanded a [[Battalion/Legends|battalion]] in the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] group [[Rusher's Brigade]], under the banner of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Daiman]].<ref name="KE" /> Centuries later, [[Maygo/Legends|"Plug-Eye" Maygo]], was hired as a [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] by the [[Kintan Gunrunners]], a group of [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]].<ref name="RFT" /> When working on their own, Sanyassans typically became [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] or [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], though some exceptionally cunning individuals became [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]].<ref name="UAA" />

Around [[96 BBY]],<ref name="CSWESan" /> the Marauders, a large group of space pirates that consisted of several dozen members,<ref name="BFE" /> hijacked a spacecraft and struck out to scour the Moddell sector. Unable to operate their advanced vessel, they crash-landed on the Forest Moon of Endor.<ref name="dbmar" /> There, they built themselves a gloomy [[Terak's Keep|fortress]], ruling over a section of the Endorian plains known as the [[Dragon's Pelt/Legends|Dragon's Pelt]] savanna. Those Sanyassans armed themselves with poorly maintained blasters and more conventional weapons. The arms gave the Marauders a technological advantage over most other species on Endor.<ref name="ISWU" /> Amongst the castaway Sanyassans were Terak, the fightmaster [[Jorak]], the scholar [[Szingo]], the smooth-skinned [[Indar (Marauder)|Indar]]<ref name="SWG" /> and the diminutive Yavid.<ref name="dbYavid" /> Some of the stranded Sanyassans, like [[Macchbraus]], chose not to pledge their loyalty to their fellow Marauders. They were marginalized, and some of them went to live in the [[Orphaned Marauder's Cave]], located near the [[Mertuen Forest]].<ref name="SWG" /> All in all, the number of Sanyassans on Endor never made up more than one percent of its sentient inhabitants.<ref name="GORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref>

[[File:Marauder_Rider.jpg|thumb|left|A Sanyassan on horseback]]
The Sanyassans of Endor domesticated local creatures such as [[Horse/Legends|horses]] and large reptilian [[Blurrg/Legends|blurrgs]] to use as beast of burden or mounts.<ref name="BFE" /> The Marauders' leader was the self-appointed King Terak, who ruled over the others by virtue of his size and strength. He was assisted by [[Charal]], a rogue [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomiri]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] who could turn into a [[Raven/Legends|raven]] thanks to her [[Talisman of the Raven|magic ring]].<ref name="ISWU" /> The commander of the Marauder [[Troop/Legends|troops]] was General Yavid, a dwarf Sanyassan who formulated the battle strategies that kept the Marauders' lands from being overrun.<ref name="BFE" /> The Marauders were perpetual enemies of the diminutive [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], a species native to Endor whose villages the Marauders frequently raided. At some point, they were also enemies of other local species like the [[Phlog/Legends|Phlogs]] and the [[Dulok/Legends|Duloks]]. They clashed with [[Morag]] the [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] witch, although Yavid orchestrated a tentative peace with her at some point.<ref name="dbYavid" />

Around the year [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]], the Marauders captured a shipwrecked humanoid scout named [[Salak Weet]]. They misunderstood Weet's references to the power generator for his ship, thinking he was talking about a mystical power source that could make them rulers of the galaxy. The Marauders imprisoned and eventually killed Weet in an attempt to learn the secret of "the Power."<ref name="dbmar" /> Some time after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Pfilbee Jhorn]] of the Galactic Empire was requisitioned for [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] second expeditionary mission to Endor. As records officer, Jhorn reported all of the scouting team's discoveries, including their encounter with the Marauders, who [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] the Imperials. Jhorn's report was one of the most thorough accounts of the Sanyassan Marauders, albeit filled with [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] bias.<ref name="ISWU" /> One year [[3 ABY/Legends|later]], during a [[Raid on Bright Tree Village|raid]] on the Ewok settlement known as [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]], the Marauders captured many Ewoks including [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]]. They also captured a young Human named [[Cindel Towani]], and killed the rest of [[Towani family|her family]], who were themselves castaways on Endor. The Marauders also stole the [[crystal oscillator]] from the Towanis' damaged spaceship. Warrick and Towani soon escaped, finding their way to the [[Noa Briqualon's hut|cottage]] of [[Noa Briqualon]], Weet's Human partner. Warrick and Briqualon's friend [[Teek (Teek)|Teek]], a member of the [[Teek/Legends|Teek]] species, helped the two stranded Humans [[Battle of Endor (Ewok–Sanyassan conflict)|defeat]] the Marauders, retrieve the parts needed to repair Briqualon and Weet's spaceship, and kill Terak.<ref name="BFE" /> With her [[Ring/Legends|ring]] destroyed, Charal was trapped in her raven form.<ref name="EGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> In the resulting power vacuum, General Yavid tried to take the Marauder throne, but he was not able to match Terak's feat of keeping order over such a rabble, and the Marauders turned on one another, foiling Yavid's bid for power.<ref name="dbYavid" /> Yet that civil war was not the end of the Marauders: Terak's son, the physically similar and equally brutal [[Zakul]], eventually emerged victorious, reestablished order, and became king.<ref name="GORW" />

[[File:Blurrgtrader.png|thumb|A Sanyassan blurrg merchant]]
In spite of the Marauders' presence, [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine chose to build the [[SLD-26 planetary shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] for his [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] on the Forest Moon.<ref name="Death Star II in the Databank">{{DB|location|deathstarii|Death Star II}}</ref> A few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] later, in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Battle of Endor/Legends|destroyed]] the battle station and [[Space warfare/Legends|defeated]] the Empire above Endor.<ref name="Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Following this decisive Alliance victory,<ref name="NEC 124">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the famed [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency sought to capitalize on the Moddell sector's sudden fame by offering to take passengers to the Forest Moon aboard their brand-new [[StarSpeeder 3000]] transports.<ref name="CSWESS3000">{{CSWECite|III|189|Starspeeder 3000}}</ref> During one of such voyages on Endor, the spacecraft team was assaulted by two green-skinned Sanyassans. [[Unidentified bald Sanyassan assailant|One]] of them threatened the Star Tours employees while [[Unidentified black-haired Sanyassan assailant|the other]] kept a lookout, armed with a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]].<ref name="EndorModdell" /><ref name="CDD">{{SW|url=news/convenient-daily-departures-the-history-of-star-tours|text=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of ''Star Tours''|int=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours|nolive=1}}</ref> However, when [[Agent/Legends|agents]] of the New Republic&mdash;the democratic government [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|established]] by the Alliance&mdash;were sent to scout the Endorian forest, they found no trace of the Sanyassan Marauders.<ref name="FF10">{{FactFile|10|END 1-4|The Forest Moon of Endor}}</ref>

At some point after the rise of the New Republic, a white-bearded Sanyassan [[Unidentified Sanyassan merchant|merchant]] sold [[Blurrg/Legends|blurrgs]] in the [[Coruscant Livestock Exchange and Exhibition]], the largest livestock fair in the galaxy. He was seen bartering with a [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] potential customer, trying to convince the customer not to buy another merchant's [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]], with a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] and a [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]] witch beside him. The merchant wore fine clothes that were similar to those of the [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] Terak. His likeness was reproduced in the [[Lyrre T'enna's annotated field guide|annotated field journal]] of [[Lyrre T'enna]], a famous [[Zoologist/Legends|zoologist]].<ref name="WFG">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The second ''[Ewok]'' film took a darker turn, as a band of deadly Marauders&mdash;aliens marooned on Endor&mdash;kills Cindel's family, leaving her with no one except her Ewok friends.|"Ewok Adventures" on [[StarWars.com]]|<ref name="Ewok Adventures">{{SWArchive|url=eu/tv/classic/f20000824/index.html|text=Ewok Adventures: A Television Adventure|date=2000-08-24}}</ref>}}
[[File:Sanyassans_concept_art.png|thumb|left|200px|Concept art featuring the original tridactyl Sanyassans]]
The Sanyassan species was created for the [[1985]] made-for-TV film ''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]''.<ref name="BFE" /> They were designed by the American director and artist [[Joe Johnston]], based on an idea by [[Jim Wheat|Jim]] and [[Ken Wheat]]. Johnston first envisioned the brutish Marauders as three-fingered and completely hairless,<ref name="ISWU" /><ref name="Wheat">{{WebCite|url=http://www.scriptsecrets.net/articles/kwheat.htm|text=Ken Wheat -- He Knows What Scares You|author=William C. Martell|archivedate=20191002073413}}</ref> but the design was changed later in pre-production, and the costumes used in the actual movie had four-fingered hands and manes of greasy hair.<ref name="BFE" /> However, many of the early Sanyassans concept sketches were reused in the Endor chapter of ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' in [[1995]], thus bringing the bald and tridactyl Sanyassans back into [[canon]].<ref name="ISWU" />

The Sanyassan Marauders of Endor also appeared in the now defunct ''[[Star Wars]]''-themed [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''.<ref name="SWG" /> Their in-game appearance was designed by character artist [[Jason Temujin Minor]].<ref name="MinorWeb">{{WebCite|url=http://www.barakastudios.com/minor.htm|text=Jason Temujin Minor's portfolio|work=Baraka Studios|archivedate=20040222074855}}</ref> The [[Sayormi]] from the [[Dead Forest (Kashyyyk)|Dead Forest]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], another race that appeared in ''Star Wars Galaxies'', closely resemble Sanyassans&mdash;not only do the Sayormi share the same character models as the Sanyassans, but they also have the same type of martial culture. Nevertheless their exact relationship has not yet been explored. ''Galaxies'' developers originally considered adding a Marauder "Heroic Encounter" to the game, which would have involved King Terak. A painting of Terak would have been added as a redeemable decorative item for completing the encounter. However, that part of the game was never implemented, although the painting could still be found in the game files.<ref name="SWG" />

In the early years of the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], the species was only known as the "Marauders." The name "Sanyassan" was first coined in ''[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]'', an article published in [[Star Wars Gamer 9|''Star Wars Gamer'' 9]] on [[March 1]], [[2002]]. From that moment on, the use of the term "Marauders" has been restricted to the group of Sanyassan pirates who crash landed on Endor.<ref name="EndorModdell" /> [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], which was published [[2001|one year before]] the first occurrences of the name "Sanyassan," still listed the species' true name as unknown, even in scientific circles.<ref name="EGAS" />

[[File:Scan_for_Sanyassan.jpg|thumb|right|The wanted poster of the "Endorian Marauder" in ''Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas'']]
The [[1993]] book ''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]'' contained the wanted poster of a criminal known as the "Marauder of Endor," described as a "known associate of Terak."<ref name="M&AGL">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref> The Marauder of Endor greatly resembles a card-playing [[Unidentified black-mustachioed Sanyassan|black-mustachioed Sanyassan]] who appeared in ''Ewoks: The Battle for Endor''.<ref name="BFE" /> The poster featured many jocular statements, including a mention of [[Wikipedia:Thanksgiving|Thanksgiving]]. The wanted Marauder was said to have "[[Mushroom/Legends|mushrooms]] lining eyebrows," "shaved dimples on both elbows" and a "[[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of his third [[Parent/Legends|mother]] on the right forelock."<ref name="M&AGL" /> The concept of "third mother" would imply Sanyassans had a different [[Wikipedia:Kinship terminology|kinship terminology]] than Humans. However, [[Leland Chee]], arbiter of the [[Holocron continuity database]] at [[Lucasfilm]], indicated that information from this book is considered non-canonical unless reused in later publications.<ref name="TT1">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=690#14724917|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-05-03|time=5:45 PM|quote=Unless referred to by a source that is in-continuity, the information is non-continuity. With that said, if it makes sense for an author to incorporate some of that information into continuity, I wouldn't stop them.}}</ref>

''The Illustrated Star Wars Universe'' and the ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' are in conflict on how old Sanyassans could get. While the former source stated that the Marauders were already adults when they crashed on Endor one hundred years before the Galactic Civil War&mdash;making them supercentenarians<ref name="ISWU" />&mdash;the latter gave an average lifespan of only seventy years.<ref name="UAA" />

Throughout the Expanded Universe, minor inconsistencies appeared regarding the Sanyassans' number of digits and shape of the ears. While sources usually portray Sanyassans with four fingers on each hand&mdash;following ''Ewoks: The Battle for Endor''&mdash; "Plug-Eye" Maygo was shown to have five-fingered hands in [[Race for the Tessent]], an article in ''[[Star Wars Gamer]] 9''.<ref name="RFT" /> In the reference book [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], a Sanyassan was depicted as having elf-like ears,<ref name="EGAS" /> akin to those of the Sephi species from Thustra,<ref name="JY" /> while all the Marauders in the movie had Human-like auricles.<ref name="BFE" />
